# Update plan pricing, invite expiration, and Arabic display names

Label: ready-for-agent

## Problem Statement

Plan pricing needs to reflect the current commercial decision. Team invites currently have no expiration metadata or lifecycle rule. The display-name formatter removes non-ASCII characters, causing Arabic names to appear blank or incomplete.

## Solution

Set the Pro plan price to 15 while keeping the Team plan at 40. Give every invite an `expires_at` value 14 days after creation and treat the invite as expired after that point. Preserve Arabic and other Unicode characters in display names while retaining sensible trimming and title/casing behavior for Latin names.

## User Stories

1. As a customer, I want the Pro plan to cost 15 per seat, so that billing reflects the current price.
2. As a customer, I want the Team plan to remain 40 per seat, so that an unchanged plan is not accidentally repriced.
3. As a customer, I want displayed plan prices to use the updated Pro and unchanged Team values, so that pricing is consistent wherever plans are shown or calculated.
4. As an inviter, I want a newly created invite to include an expiration timestamp, so that its validity is explicit.
5. As an inviter, I want invites to expire 14 days after creation, so that pending access does not remain open indefinitely.
6. As the invite service, I want expiration to be calculated from the service clock and creation time, so that behavior is deterministic and testable.
7. As the system, I want the expiration rule to use the same time basis as invite creation, so that boundary comparisons are reliable.
8. As a recipient, I want an expired invite to be recognized as expired, so that I cannot rely on stale access instructions.
9. As a user with an Arabic name, I want my full display name to remain readable, so that the guest list does not show a blank name.
10. As a user with a Unicode name, I want supported characters preserved during shortening, so that formatting does not discard my identity.
11. As a user with a Latin name, I want existing readable title formatting to remain intact, so that this fix does not regress current display behavior.
12. As a maintainer, I want pricing, invite expiry, and display-name behavior covered by focused external-behavior tests, so that future changes are safe.

## Implementation Decisions

- Update the centralized plan-price values: Pro is 15; Team remains 40; Free remains unchanged.
- Preserve the existing per-seat pricing behavior and apply the updated values through the existing pricing interface.
- Add `expires_at` to the invite data model.
- Set `expires_at` to exactly 14 days after `created_at` when an invite is created.
- Use the invite service's injected clock for expiration calculation and comparisons.
- Define an invite as expired once the current time is at or beyond `expires_at`; retain the existing invite creation flow unless a later requirement adds enforcement or notification behavior.
- Replace ASCII-only display-name conversion with Unicode-safe handling. Truncation must not turn Arabic characters into an empty string; preserve valid Unicode text and keep existing Latin formatting behavior where applicable.
- Do not change the Team price to 45; that earlier note was explicitly withdrawn.
- Do not use a 7-day expiration; that earlier note was explicitly superseded by 14 days.

## Testing Decisions

- Test Pro and Team per-seat prices through the public pricing function, including confirmation that Team remains 40.
- Test invite creation with a fixed clock and verify both `created_at` and `expires_at`, including the exact 14-day interval.
- Test expiration boundary behavior at the expiration timestamp and immediately before it through the highest existing invite-service seam available.
- Test Arabic display names remain non-empty and preserve their characters after formatting and length limiting.
- Retain the existing Latin title-formatting test to prevent regressions.
- Prefer the existing unit-test module and public functions/services; assert observable values rather than implementation details.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the Free plan price.
- Changing the Team plan price from 40.
- Seven-day expiration rules.
- Adding invite resend, revocation, cleanup jobs, notifications, or UI changes beyond representing and recognizing expiration.
- Changing name translations, transliteration, locale-specific capitalization, or unrelated Unicode normalization policy.

## Further Notes

The later corrections in the request are authoritative: invite expiration is 14 days, and the Team plan remains 40. This spec is documentation only; implementation is for the assigned agent in a subsequent workflow.
